hero.label: Xiaohongshu image text OCR tool
hero.title: Pull the value out of Xiaohongshu image cards, all at once
hero.description: Image notes increasingly bake the steps, book lists, prices, and specs into image cards, leaving the body with a line or two. You can see the text but can't copy it. MediaClaw's built-in image text extraction (OCR) reads the cover and every image, writes the text back to the collected record, and carries it through copy and export.

why.subtitle: Why MediaClaw
why.title: Why not phone screenshots or online OCR
why.description: The three old paths each stall on something, batch, accuracy, or moving images by hand. The real problem is the same: image text is disconnected from the note data you're already collecting.

items.title: Batch, not one image at a time
items.description: Phone screenshot text grabs one image at a time and can't be merged with the note's title, body, and comments. Image text extraction reads the whole note and lands results in one record.

items.title: Paid model, more accurate
items.description: Free OCR is inconsistent; complex layouts, stylized fonts, and vertical text produce errors. One wrong character in a price, title, or spec means rework. Image text extraction uses a paid model that's steadier.

items.title: No moving images by hand
items.description: Online OCR sites make you save and upload each image yourself, back to the manual grind. Image text extraction reads the collected note directly and skips the shuffle.

items.question: Xiaohongshu makes the value into images, how do I extract the text?
items.answer: OCR the images. After collecting the note with MediaClaw, run image text extraction on it; the extension reads the cover and every image one by one and writes text back to the record for copy or export. OCR is a paid capability billed by quota; collection and CSV/Excel export are free.

items.question: Can cover and image text be batch-extracted into copyable text?
items.answer: Yes. Image text extraction reads the cover plus every image in a note, not just one, and writes results back to the record as text that carries through CSV or Markdown export for full-copy and search.

items.question: Free online OCR works too, why use the extension's paid OCR?
items.answer: Free online OCR is inconsistent; complex images, stylized fonts, and vertical text produce errors, one wrong character in a price, title, or spec means rework, and you still save and upload each image by hand. MediaClaw's image text extraction reads the collected note directly with a paid model for higher accuracy. It's the tradeoff between free-but-maybe-wrong and paid-but-more-accurate; pick the latter for sensitive content.

items.question: Where does the extracted image text live?
items.answer: It writes back to the collected record inside the extension, alongside the note's title, body, and engagement. Run OCR on the record and the result lands right there, ready to copy or export to CSV/Markdown, with no external tools.
